soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1 / def:exposed-order
soundness_flags.one_line: The theorem permits beta>d, but k_star is defined up to beta, so binom(d,k_star)=0 when k_star>d and the displayed zero risk bound is impossible for nonzero lower-order effects; define the exposed order over 1,...,min(beta,d) (or assume beta<=d).

soundness_flags.label: def:block-family / Theorem 1 lower bound
soundness_flags.one_line: The alleged fuzzy family does not define the two opposite mean tilts or their amplitudes/distributions, so Pi^{blk} is not a determinate least-favourable family capable of witnessing the stated minimax lower bound.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v4, 5 February 2024; cited journal primary is Journal of Causal Inference 11(1), 20220051, whose official HTML was inaccessible during review
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 16–18, Theorems 1–2 and discussion immediately following Theorem 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible author version states a SNIPE variance upper bound with degree-polynomial scaling, a lower bound Omega(1/(n p^beta)) without degree dependence, and explicitly attributes the degree gap to weak analysis.
The paper gives a design-based Riesz framework with necessary and sufficient conditions for unbiasedness and consistency and conservative variance estimation.
The paper studies TTE estimation with unknown network structure under heterogeneous additive network effects and uses average historical baseline measurements.
The paper introduces a general-design pseudoinverse estimator, gives bias and variance bounds, and evaluates clustered Bernoulli and complete-randomization designs.
The paper proposes covariate-adjusted low-order-interference estimators, proves asymptotic no-harm variance, and gives an asymptotically conservative variance estimator.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace k_star by max{r<=min(beta,d):Delta_r(p)≠0}, and state the beta>d reduction explicitly before retaining the p=1/2 corollary.
Specify the two fuzzy priors in Pi^{blk}: the tilt magnitude, prior law on signs, the induced TTE separation, and the divergence bound used by the lower-bound route.

Either justify the l1 coefficient envelope as a realistic new condition or prove the same rate under the published bounded-outcome class, so the advertised strict tightening has a directly comparable model class.

recommended_next_step: Revise the exposed-order domain and fully construct the fuzzy block priors, then rerun novelty review with a source-verified comparison of the l1-envelope class to the published bounded-outcome class.
